newsitem.title: USA: Conn. rules against Northeast rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Conn. rules against Northeast rate hike.

text.p: Connecticut's Department of Public Utility Control (DPUC) ruled Friday against a Northeast Utilities request to raise electricity rates to help cover losses from its idled Millstone nuclear power plants.
The three Millstone units, with a total generating capacity of nearly 2,700 megawatts (MW), have been shut since early 1996 amid safety concerns.
Northeast said their loss has cost the utility an estimated $990 million in replacement power costs and other outage-related items.
DPUC's five commissioners unanimously ruled Northeast was not entitled to raise its rates because it had not acted prudently in its operation of the Millstone facility.
Northeast officials said earlier this week they were asking the DPUC to approve a $340 million rate increase to its electricity customers.

"It's just too apparent, too clear, that Northeast Utilities' management of its nuclear facilities adds up to a long, long history of imprudence," said DPUC commissioner Janet Polinsky, adding "Mistakes were made, lots of them."
"They had ample opportunity on many occasions to make decisions that would not have led to the condition they are in today," said DPUC commisioner Glenn Arthur.

The DPUC's ruling has the force of law, but Northeast Utilities spokeswoman Myra Humphries confirmed immediately following the meeting that the company would file an appeal with the Superior Court of Connecticut within the next 45 days.
The DPUC also ruled Friday that Northeast may at a later date seek recovery through higher rates of up to $40 million of investments needed to improve the reliability of the company's power system.

The commission's ruling against Northeast was in response to a motion arguing Northeast had not acted prudently in management of its Millstone facility and therefore was not entitled to a rate increase.
The motion was filed jointly last week by the state attorney general, the Office of Consumer Counsel, and the prosecutorial division of the DPUC.
